//: ACP-439. Which dossier rows each finding kind cites, by the framework's own clause as Annex E (dossier/annexes/E-control-mapping.md) or the MITRE chapter (dossier/02-THREAT-MODEL-MITRE.md) spells it. Chosen sparsely: the two to four rows a security reader would open, not every row that could be argued. The status printed beside each citation is NEVER stored here: it is read from the dossier at the engine pin by scripts/embed-annex.mjs. src/report/controls.test.ts asserts every citation below resolves to a row of that generated data, so a renamed row turns the build red. A kind mapped to [] cites nothing on purpose: it reports what this scan could not look at, and no framework row is about that. EU AI Act Art. 14(5) and DORA Art. 11(1) are never cited: src/report/controls.ts EXCLUDED_CITATIONS gives the reason for each, and a test holds this file to it.

mitre_position_status.//: The MITRE chapter grades a technique by a position phrase, not by Annex E's vocabulary, and ControlRef's status field admits only the annex's six words. This table is the one place a position phrase is given a status word, for --json only: the terminal prints the chapter's own phrase. 'Out of scope by design.' maps to 'not covered' because, for a person reading a scan, the engine does not constrain that technique. A cited row whose phrase is missing here fails src/report/controls.test.ts.
